places.name: Nitto Tatara
places.connection: One of the few remaining operational traditional 'tatara' iron forges in Japan, offering a glimpse into the technology of Irontown.

places.name: Nippon Television Network (NTV) Headquarters
places.connection: NTV was a major production partner for the film, providing significant funding and broadcast support.

places.name: Tokuma Shoten Publishing
places.connection: The original parent company of Studio Ghibli and a key financier and producer of the film.

places.name: Shiratani Unsuikyo Ravine, Yakushima Island
places.connection: A primary visual inspiration for the film's ancient, moss-covered forests.

places.name: Shirakami-Sanchi
places.connection: This UNESCO World Heritage site, a vast mountain range of virgin beech forest, was another key inspiration for the film's natural landscapes.

places.name: Studio Ghibli
places.connection: The animation studio where Princess Mononoke was written, storyboarded, and produced.

places.name: Ghibli Museum
places.connection: Museum dedicated to the art and animation of Studio Ghibli, where production materials from the film are often displayed.

places.name: Walter Reade Theater, Lincoln Center
places.connection: Venue for the film's U.S. premiere at the New York Film Festival on October 8, 1999.

places.name: TIFF Bell Lightbox
places.connection: The central venue for the Toronto International Film Festival, where the film had its North American premiere in September 1999.

places.name: Sugaya Tatara Sannai
places.connection: A preserved historic 'tatara' (traditional Japanese iron smelter), representing the technology used by Lady Eboshi's Irontown.

places.name: Hiraizumi
places.connection: A town in the Tōhoku region, the historical homeland of the Emishi people from whom the protagonist Ashitaka descends.

places.name: Nippon Television (NTV) Headquarters
places.connection: The headquarters of the film's main production partner and financier.

places.name: Toho Studios
places.connection: The main studio lot and headquarters of Toho, the film's Japanese distributor.

places.name: Yakushima Island
places.connection: The primary real-world inspiration for the film's ancient, moss-covered forests. Miyazaki and his team scouted this location extensively.

places.name: Shiratani Unsuikyo Ravine
places.connection: A specific, popular trail on Yakushima Island famous for its ancient cedar trees and dense moss, which directly inspired the look of the Forest Spirit's domain.

places.name: Shirakami-Sanchi
places.connection: A UNESCO World Heritage site known for its vast, pristine beech forests, which also served as a key visual reference for the film's natural environments.

places.name: Izumo Province (Historic)
places.connection: This region was the historical center of 'tatara' iron sand smelting in Japan, the very industry depicted in Lady Eboshi's Irontown.

places.name: Studio Ghibli
places.connection: The animation studio where 'Princess Mononoke' was conceived, storyboarded, and animated.

places.name: Tōhoku Region
places.connection: The historical homeland of the Emishi people, the tribe from which Prince Ashitaka originates.

places.name: El Capitan Theatre
places.connection: Site of the film's United States premiere on October 29, 1999.

places.name: Yakushima Island
places.connection: UNESCO site; Miyazaki research location

places.name: Shiratani Unsuikyo, Yakushima
places.connection: Mossy forest inspiration
